It is not generally accepted that an individual may force their will on others, how do groups of people gain the right to do so when acting through government?

Idealistic: The individual does not have this authority but the collective does, the individuals in government have power as long as they are acting for the collective as opposed to themselves, restricted to the space of areas that impact the collective.

Cynical: Government gains authority by being able to shoot you. The authority of individuals in government extends as far as they can exercise it without being reigned in by other government officials or triggering a mass revolt.

The justification for power existing in a group as far as it affects the whole group is just a generalization of the first principle.

No individual may force their will on others, so when there's a conflict the collective of individuals decide.
